title: Singapore's Performance for PM2.5, PM10, Sulphur Dioxide, Ozone, Nitrogen Dioxide and Carbon Monoxide Emissions
what_it_is: Singapore's Performance for PM2.5, PM10, Sulphur Dioxide, Ozone, Nitrogen Dioxide and Carbon Monoxide Emissions

sections.label: Singapore air quality 2021-2022
sections.summary: Singapore's air quality was Good or Moderate on 99.5% of days in 2021 and 100% in 2022, meeting 2020 targets for several pollutants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: In 2021 and 2022, Singapore's air quality was in the "Good" or "Moderate" range 99.5% and 100% of the days, respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Singapore has met the 2020 air quality targets for nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide and fine particulate matter PM2.5.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: PM10 and ozone continue to be a challenge due to multiple factors, including the weather and complex chemical reactions between the pollutants and the environment – that refers to ozone.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We will continue to review our air quality targets as well as policies to address local pollutant emissions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: For example, the emission standards for motorcycles and existing industrial plants were further tightened this year.

sections.label: PM2.5 targets met
sections.summary: Air quality in 2021 and 2022 both met the 2020 air quality targets for PM2.5.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: First of all, I would like to reiterate that our air quality for 2021 and 2022 both met the 2020 air quality targets for PM2.5.

sections.label: PM2.5 targets and review
sections.summary: Singapore met PM2.5 targets with no prolonged over concentration, and the suggestion to continually review targets is right.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: As I have mentioned, we have met the PM2.5 quality targets and, therefore, we do not have a prolonged over concentration or exposure to PM2.5 in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Having said that, I think the suggestion to review our targets continually, given new information coming from the medical and health scientific communities, is the right one.
